research.instructions: Did research identify an established 1-D transport reference implementation with an equation/unit/boundary mapping, or explicitly document a search and rationale for none?

criteria.true: A named reference with mapping and limits, or a documented search/rationale.
criteria.false: Reference handling is silent or omitted.

research.instructions: Does the artifact mark external sources (papers, books, code repositories) as READ only where the handoff lists a concrete command or fetch performed in this session, and otherwise as not read / known-of? Any claim of having inspected code or read a book without such evidence is a failure.

criteria.true: Every read/unread label is consistent with the listed commands; unverified sources are labelled unread.
criteria.false: The artifact claims to have read or inspected a source with no evidence of access.

research.instructions: Are the analytic verification fixtures mathematically correct and internally consistent: geometry matches the label (cylindrical vs slab), boundary conditions are physically appropriate (zero flux at the axis, Dirichlet at the edge), and the closed-form solution satisfies the stated equation and boundary conditions?

criteria.true: Each fixture's equation, BCs, and solution are consistent and correct.
criteria.false: At least one fixture has a wrong geometry, BC, or solution.

research.instructions: Does the artifact stay within the research stage's brief: correct unit name (d2-profiles), under the requested length, no physics claims beyond cited or derived content, and no implementation decisions presented as settled?

criteria.true: Labels, length and claims match the brief.
criteria.false: Wrong unit labels, over length, or unsupported claims.

spec.instructions: Is the five-part scientific package complete and bound to the proposal: verification test (analytic fixtures with tolerances), experimental validation plan, uncertainty model, domain of validity, reference comparison pathway (TORAX mapping)?

criteria.true: All five parts exist as named artifacts with content, versioned and referenced from the main spec.
criteria.false: One or more parts is missing, empty, or unbound.

spec.instructions: Does the spec leave every 0.1.0 constant, assumption and equation unchanged for the profile-off path, and route the 0.1.0->0.2.0 change through a draft change-request listing affected assumption IDs, old/new behaviour and rationale?

criteria.true: Profile-off path declared bit-for-bit identical; a change-request draft lists affected IDs with old/new and rationale.
criteria.false: A constant/assumption change is implied without a change-request, or the profile-off guarantee is missing.

spec.instructions: Does the spec resolve the three research-stage decisions with explicit values and rationale: transport-coefficient form, 0-D/1-D integral tolerance, edge boundary condition (and its interaction with the equilibrium solver's unsupported status)?

criteria.true: All three are decided with numbers and reasons.
criteria.false: At least one is left open or stated without a value.

spec.instructions: Are the governing equations dimensionally consistent, with the flux-surface Jacobian V'(rho) treated correctly, boundary conditions (zero flux at axis, stated edge condition) matching the fixtures, and volume integrals defined so that they reduce to the existing 0-D N, We, Wi balances?

criteria.true: Equations, units, BCs and integrals are mutually consistent and reduce to the 0-D model.
criteria.false: A dimensional, Jacobian, BC or integral inconsistency is present.

spec.instructions: Are prescribed transport coefficients and unread deposition shapes (ECH, gas) explicitly labelled illustrative/uncalibrated with ranges, never presented as calibrated DIII-D physics?

criteria.true: Every modelling choice is labelled illustrative with ranges and provenance.
criteria.false: A modelling choice is presented as validated or calibrated.

design-review.instructions: Consider AC-5 and AC-6 in spec section 12 and D2-VER-STEADY, EIGEN-DIRICHLET, EIGEN-REFLECT, MMS-CONDUCTION and REFINEMENT in verification section 3. Do they state fixture inputs, exact expected solutions, numeric tolerances, convergence-rate bands and pass/fail rules so the tests could be written without a scientific choice?

criteria.true: Fixture and convergence criteria are executable as written.
criteria.false: A fixture or rate criterion lacks an input, expected value, tolerance or rule.

design-review.instructions: Consider AC-3, AC-4 and AC-7 in spec section 12 and D2-VER-PARITY and D2-VER-LEDGER in verification section 3. Do they state the compared quantities, the relative or absolute formula, numeric tolerances, the perturbation rejection bound and pass/fail rules?

criteria.true: Conservation criteria are executable as written.
criteria.false: A conservation criterion lacks a formula, tolerance or rule.

design-review.instructions: Consider AC-1, AC-2, AC-8, AC-9 and AC-10 in spec section 12 and D2-VER-FAILSAFE, DIAGNOSTICS and OFFPATH in verification section 3. Do they fix the case sets, option field names, error-message grammar, driver path, sample times, tolerances and objective pass/fail rules, leaving no structural choice to Software?

criteria.true: Interface and process criteria are objective and fixed.
criteria.false: A case set, name, grammar, path or rule is left to implementation or is subjective.

design-review.instructions: Does the approved change request specs/change-requests/D2-PROFILES-001.json satisfy specs/change-requests/README.md: assumption IDs, old/new behaviour, units, reason, affected tests, compatibility, new model version, physics agent identity, Director decision, and SHA-256 bindings for the spec and all six package artifacts, with every open question in the DRAFT resolved by a recorded DD-n decision?

criteria.true: All README fields present, hashes bound, no OPEN items remain.
criteria.false: A required field, a hash, or an unresolved OPEN item is present.

design-review.instructions: Given DD-1..DD-15, could a software lane implement the profile-on path in physics/ and tests/ only, with the profile-off path bit-for-bit unchanged, using the numerical scheme (s8), boundary conditions (s7), source distributions (s6, DD-12 cell-centre evaluation) and the verification-only kernel entry, without touching python/ or altering any 0.1.0 constant?

criteria.true: Scheme, interfaces, file scope and off-path guarantee are specified precisely enough to implement.
criteria.false: A missing interface, ambiguous scheme detail, or an unavoidable 0.1.0 change blocks implementation.

design-review.instructions: Are physics 0.2.0 (profiles on), verification 0.3.0, profile-off modelVersion 0.1.0, schemaVersion 1 both on and off, and registry top-level 0.1.0 stated the same way in the spec, the verification document and the change request?

criteria.true: No version or schema statement disagrees between the three artifacts.
criteria.false: At least one artifact carries a different or superseded version statement.

design-review.instructions: Compare the numeric content of AC-5 (1e-3 plus rate bands), AC-6 (dt levels, order bands), AC-9 (driver, nine-case grid, 128 corners) and AC-1 (six control sets) between spec section 12, verification section 3 and the change request proposedTolerances. Do the numbers and case sets agree?

criteria.true: The same numbers and case sets appear in all three artifacts.
criteria.false: A number or case set differs between artifacts.

design-review.instructions: Is every item marked as decided by a DD-n decision free of OPEN, pending, 'to confirm', 'to decide', 'Director to' or 'Software finalises/documents' wording in the spec, verification document and change request? Historical notes that say a value WAS changed by a decision do not count as open markers.

criteria.true: No open marker remains on a decided item.
criteria.false: An open marker remains on a decided item.
